extension.description: A Kodi metadata scraper for movies and TV shows, backed by your self-hosted Chronicle server. Unlike a normal scraper, it never talks to TMDB or any other upstream source directly -- it only ever asks Chronicle, which resolves-and-creates the item through whichever metadata providers you've already configured there, so Kodi always ends up seeing exactly what Chronicle itself would show for that title -- movie sets, seasons and episodes, multi-source ratings, trailers and all. Distinct from Chronicle_Scrobbler (which reports watch progress) -- this addon supplies library metadata during "Change Content" / library scans.
extension.news: v2.6.0 - Two more real bugs found and fixed during the v2.5.0 library-wide rebuild, both confirmed via live evidence, not guessed: (1) movie_art_sync's fast VideoLibrary-lookup path had no folder validation at all -- unlike the source-browsing fallback (already tightened in v2.5.0's predecessor fix), it blindly trusted whatever file Kodi's own title index returned for a search title. Caught live: "X" (2022) wrote its own correct art into the "X-Men (2000)" folder, because Kodi's stored title for that entry was ALSO still wrong (a self-reinforcing corruption -- Kodi's local-NFO-wins behaviour kept re-importing a stale NFO's wrong title on every touch, undoing a direct database correction each time, until the stale NFO itself was deleted). The fast path now verifies the returned file's own folder actually matches the searched title(+year) before trusting it, exactly like the slow path already did. (2) collection_sync now repairs stale set-art registrations, not just missing ones. Confirmed ~110 movie sets (out of ~177) had art registered against a share path ("Movie Collections" on an old share) that no longer exists at all following an earlier NAS reorganisation -- Kodi registers a set's art once and never re-checks it, so these showed permanently blank no matter how many times Chronicle correctly filled in art at the new location, since collection_sync only ever handled the MISSING case. Every sync_collection_art call now also verifies each of Kodi's own currently-registered local art paths still exists; a dead one gets repointed at the same-named file in the current set folder if one exists there, or cleared outright if not -- never left silently dangling. v2.5.0 - Adds the actual bulk mechanism the v2.4.0 NFO setting needed: "Rebuild local NFOs from Chronicle" (main addon menu, and an action button in Settings -> Local Files). The passive per-scrape NFO write can only ever help NEW movies -- it can't retroactively fix a library where local NFOs already exist, since Kodi never invokes this scraper for those at all. This action deletes every local .nfo and movieset-* file the whole movie library currently has, then forces a refresh per movie so Chronicle_Scraper gets invoked and repopulates them fresh -- i.e. exactly the manual delete-then-refresh procedure already run once by hand this session, now built into the addon itself. Shows a clear warning (irreversible, other tools' local data will be lost, can take a long time) and requires explicit confirmation before doing anything; a progress dialog allows cancelling mid-run. New shared lib/nfo_rebuild.py; movie_art_sync.py's timeout-guarded listdir helper is now public (listdir_with_timeout) so this reuses it instead of duplicating the same unresponsive-share protection. v2.4.0 - New setting (Local Files category), "Recreate local NFO file from Chronicle's data", defaulted ON. Root-caused (via the new v2.3.3 logging plus a live JSON-RPC VideoLibrary.RefreshMovie test against X-Men) why existing library items weren't picking up Chronicle's updates at all: Kodi checks for a movie's own local NFO before ever invoking this scraper, no exceptions, no settings toggle -- confirmed X-Men's ".nfo" was a real tinyMediaManager-authored file, meaning Chronicle_Scraper's find/getdetails never even ran for it on any subsequent scan, automatic or manual. Since tinyMediaManager only (re)writes an NFO when explicitly told to, a movie scraped once by it keeps that same NFO forever even as Chronicle's own data changes. Rather than fight Kodi's NFO-first behaviour, this addon now writes its own NFO every time it IS invoked (new addition, or NFO removed) using Chronicle's current data -- named to match the real video file's basename when known (e.g. "X-Men (2000).nfo"), which is confirmed to take precedence over a generic "movie.nfo" the same way a previous tool's NFO would. Refactored movie_art_sync.py's folder lookup into a shared find_movie_location() (now also surfaces the real video filename) so the new NFO writer and the existing art sync reuse a single lookup instead of each browsing the same video sources independently. v2.3.3 - Logging only, no behavior change: this addon's entire poster/collection-art path had almost no log visibility, making "why is this one movie/collection still showing a blank or stale poster" unanswerable from the log alone. Added: get_details/get_artwork now log Chronicle's full response summary (per-arttype candidate counts, whether a collection was present and whether it had a poster/backdrop) or an explicit warning when Chronicle returns nothing at all; find now logs the resolved item id/posterUrl or an explicit "no candidate" warning; apply_artwork logs exactly what gets pinned via setArt(); sync_movie_art logs the URL and destination path for every write attempt and explicitly logs when Chronicle has no candidate for a given art type; sync_collection_art now logs -- for the first time -- when a set's poster/fanart is skipped because a local file already exists (this module is fill-only and never overwrites, so a stale local file here can silently block every future update with zero prior trace) and logs the URL Chronicle currently has for that field so it can be compared against the stale file by hand. v2.3.2 - Fix (confirmed directly -- one worker thread stuck for 2+ minutes with kodi.log completely silent, while a live JSONRPC.Ping proved Kodi's own core was otherwise fully responsive): xbmcvfs.listdir() on an unresponsive SMB share doesn't raise or time out on its own, it just never returns. Since v2.3.1 expanded each multipath source into several real paths, one unresponsive share among them now means several separate chances to hang the whole scrape indefinitely instead of one. Every listdir() call in the source-browsing fallback now runs in a background thread with an 8s timeout; a share that doesn't answer in time is skipped (logged) rather than blocking the search forever. v2.3.1 - Fix (confirmed directly via kodi.log, not guessed): the v2.3.0 source-browsing fallback found the right folder name via xbmcvfs.listdir() on a multipath:// source (e.g. this user's bundled "Movies" source spanning several shares), then broke by re-appending that folder name onto the raw multipath:// string itself. multipath:// is a container Kodi's own listdir() browses transparently, not a real location -- appending a suffix to the whole bundle instead of to one of its real underlying paths produced a hard "XFILE::CDirectory::GetDirectory" error from Kodi's own core with no Python-catchable exception, so it silently looked like "no folder found" for every movie living under a multipath source whenever the VideoLibrary-lookup fast path missed (confirmed reproducible 3/3 times for The Union). Sources are now expanded into their real constituent paths up front, so nothing downstream ever builds a path against the bundle itself. v2.3.0 - movie_art_sync's cross-platform folder fallback (Files.GetSources + xbmcvfs.listdir, written in v2.2.1's development but never actually deployed) is now live. The VideoLibrary-only lookup from v2.2.1 could still miss movies that were already in the library at scan time if the title lookup didn't match cleanly (confirmed against The Union and X-Men still showing stale local posters after a rescan) -- this fallback browses the configured video sources directly by folder name instead of depending on VideoLibrary state at all. v2.2.1 - Confirmed directly (diagnostic build, not assumption) that Kodi's find/getdetails contract gives scrapers no path information on any channel -- querystring, cwd, or environment -- on any platform, since it's the same C++ core invocation everywhere. Also confirmed getartwork does not automatically follow getdetails, so movie_art_sync can't rely on it as a later retry. Added a short, early-exiting retry directly in movie_art_sync's VideoLibrary lookup to ride out the real, reproducible commit-timing race instead of silently giving up on the first miss. v2.2.0 - Added movie_art_sync: overwrites a movie's own local poster/fanart files (found via Kodi's own VideoLibrary, since the scraper contract never provides a file path) with Chronicle's current picks -- unlike collection sync, this deliberately overwrites, since the point is fixing stale leftover files from a previous scraper. Fixed collection_sync misreporting a failed image download as "folder not writable" -- only a genuine write failure implicates the folder now. v2.1.0 - Movie sets now sync into Kodi's own configured "Movie set information folder" (read live from Kodi's Settings API, never hardcoded) whenever a poster/fanart is missing there -- local folder art always wins over scraper-contributed art in Kodi, so this keeps it from silently going stale or blank when a set's local files are missing. Existing local art is never overwritten. Fixed: getdetails/getartwork now explicitly pin each item's own poster/fanart/etc via setArt() instead of only offering candidates, since Kodi doesn't reliably default-select the right one among several; the same fix applies to episode thumbnails. Added the getartwork action (movies and TV), which Kodi's own art-refresh flow calls separately from getdetails and which this addon previously silently ignored. v2.0.0 - Adds a full xbmc.metadata.scraper.tvshows extension point (show/season/episode), movie collections (Kodi movie sets, with set artwork), multi-source ratings, multi-candidate artwork, trailers, tagline/MPAA/country/studio/status, and cross-provider external IDs (IMDB/TVDB/TMDB/Trakt) -- all mined from data Chronicle already has across every configured metadata provider. Movies scraper rewritten on Kodi's modern InfoTagVideo API. v1.0.0 - Initial release: movie search/details backed by Chronicle's new /api/v1/scraper/movies endpoints. Connect to Chronicle via the same QR/PIN device-auth flow as Chronicle_Scrobbler.
